sentences.text: Nayantara Khatun vs Unknown on 6 April, 2026

Author: Tirthankar Ghosh
Bench: Tirthankar Ghosh
06.04.2026
Court No.35.
D/L. 95
 Rakib
 Crm (Db) 2986 of 2024
 In Re: An Application for cancellation of bail under Section 483(3) of
 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (corresponding to
Section 439(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973).

And
 In the matter of : Nayantara Khatun
 ......Petitioner.

Mr. Bipin Baidya
 ......for the Petitioner.
 Mr. Bidyut Kumar Roy
 Mr. Mujibar Ali Naskar.
 ..... for the State.

Mr. Mukteswar Maity
 Ms. Manika Sarkar
 ......for the respondent nos.1 to 3.
Learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the order of anticipatory bail which was granted was without any materials being effectively considered by the learned Sessions Judge.
The accusations according to the petitioner are under Sections 498A/325/313/307/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned Sessions Judge while considering the application for anticipatory bail took into account the allegations centered around the husband and thereafter was pleased to grant anticipatory bail to the accused persons.
Subsequently, the accused persons surrendered on the next date before the learned A.C.J.M., Baruipur and were granted bail.
Learned advocate for the State is present.
Learned advocate for the accused opposite parties are also present.

Having regard to the fact that the order for anticipatory bail and the consequential bail order was passed on 07.02.2024, at this belated stage after more than two years, I am not inclined to interfere with the liberty of the accused opposite parties.

With the aforesaid observations CRM (DB) 2986 of 2024 is disposed of.

(Tirthankar Ghosh, J.)
